description: This image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—across different difficulty levels of a CoT (Chain-of-Thought) task. The charts are arranged horizontally, with the “easy” chart on the left showing 40.6% for N+K+ (teal), 45.9% for N−K+ (yellow), 10.1% for N−K− (orange), and 3.3% for N+K− (red); the “medium” chart in the center shows 44.6% for N+K+ (teal), 44.3% for N−K+ (yellow), 7.2% for N−K− (orange), and 3.9% for N+K− (red); and the “hard” chart on the right shows 36.2% for N+K+ (teal), 36.8% for N−K− (orange), 20.1% for N−K+ (yellow), and 7.0% for N+K− (red). A shared legend on the right identifies the color coding for each category, and each pie slice is explicitly labeled with its percentage. The slices appear visually ordered by descending size within each chart, and no slices are exploded or emphasized beyond their standard presentation.
